periods.analysis: Harborview enters the series in a strong prevention position: childhood immunization is 96.8%, 1.8 percentage points above the >=95% target, and life expectancy is 81.6 years, above the >=80-year target. This is a green result because the basics are working: pediatric practices, school-entry review, and the Health Department’s Saturday clinic at Seaside Family Center are keeping most children current before the respiratory-virus season. The life expectancy result reflects the same prevention-first pattern, with chronic-disease screening and coastal active-living programs reaching stable participation in the East Bluff and Marina districts. We should treat this as a high-performing baseline, not a finish line.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the green result by keeping the Seaside Saturday clinic open through October and reserving walk-in vaccine slots for kindergarten and seventh-grade catch-up cases. Extend the school-nurse immunization reconciliation pilot to all Harborview Unified elementary campuses, with weekly exception lists sent to pediatric providers. Maintain quarterly review of life expectancy drivers, especially diabetes control, blood pressure screening, and preventable injury trends.

periods.analysis: Performance remains green, though childhood immunization moved down from 96.8% to 96%, a 0.8-point quarter-over-quarter decrease while still above the >=95% target. Life expectancy also moved down from 81.6 years to 81 years, remaining above the >=80-year target and still consistent with a healthy community profile. The softer quarter appears operational rather than structural: holiday travel, delayed well-child visits, and several late provider data files from the North Harbor Pediatrics group affected the December close. Prevention coverage remains broad, but the margin narrowed enough to merit disciplined follow-up.
periods.recommendations: Keep the result green by running a January catch-up list for children flagged in the school-entry registry, starting with the 312 records missing final documentation rather than assuming they are unvaccinated. Ask North Harbor Pediatrics and Bayview Children’s Clinic to submit monthly flat files by the fifth business day until data timeliness stabilizes. Continue fall-prevention and hypertension screening through senior centers, since those programs support the life expectancy measure over time.

periods.analysis: The first quarter shows a constructive rebound: childhood immunization increased from 96% to 96.5%, a 0.5-point quarter-over-quarter gain, and remains above the >=95% target. Life expectancy increased from 81 years to 81.3 years, also above the >=80-year target. The January catch-up work appears to have helped, especially in the Harborview Unified pre-K cohort and among families served by the Route 4 mobile clinic near Oyster Point. This is a green result with evidence that timely outreach can recover small slippage before it becomes a gap.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the mobile-clinic cadence on Route 4 for another quarter and add two evening vaccine blocks at the Oyster Point library branch for working caregivers. Use the immunization registry to generate a provider-level missed-opportunity report after each well-child visit batch. Keep chronic-disease prevention aligned with the same neighborhoods, pairing vaccine events with blood pressure checks and tobacco-cessation referrals.

periods.analysis: Harborview strengthened its prevention position in Q2: childhood immunization rose from 96.5% to 97.6%, a 1.1-point quarter-over-quarter increase and well above the >=95% target. Life expectancy held steady at 81.3 years, unchanged from Q1 and above the >=80-year target. The immunization gain tracks with the Spring Start campaign, which combined school reminders, pediatric portal messages, and pop-up clinics at Pier 6 Community Hall before summer camp enrollment. A steady life expectancy measure is expected quarter to quarter, and the current level continues to indicate broad population-health resilience.
periods.recommendations: Preserve the 97.6% immunization level by converting the Spring Start campaign into a standing April-May operating playbook with named clinic leads and weekly dashboard review. Extend pop-up clinics to summer camp physicals and sports clearance events so vaccination stays embedded in routine family errands. Continue monitoring life expectancy inputs through preventable hospitalization, overdose, and injury dashboards rather than waiting for the annual roll-up.

periods.analysis: Q3 remains green, but the mix shifted: childhood immunization decreased from 97.6% to 95.6%, a 2.0-point quarter-over-quarter drop, while still above the >=95% target. Life expectancy increased from 81.3 years to 81.8 years, a 0.5-year gain and comfortably above the >=80-year target. The immunization decline is likely tied to denominator growth from new family move-ins at the Harbor Landing and Saltgrass developments, plus lagging transfer records from out-of-county providers. The life expectancy improvement is encouraging, but prevention requires attention to the thinner immunization cushion.
periods.recommendations: Hold green performance by launching a New Resident Vaccine Welcome workflow with Planning and Housing so families receiving occupancy packets also get clinic locations and registry enrollment instructions. Assign two public health nurses to reconcile immunization records for Harbor Landing and Saltgrass school-zone entrants before the October census file. Continue the active-living and chronic-disease work that supports life expectancy, particularly the Bayshore walking-prescription cohort and pharmacy blood pressure checks.

periods.analysis: The objective remains green, but Q4 shows a second small immunization decline: childhood immunization moved from 95.6% to 95.4%, down 0.2 points quarter over quarter and still just above the >=95% target. Life expectancy decreased from 81.8 years to 81.3 years, a 0.5-year drop, while remaining above the >=80-year target. The data suggest Harborview is still healthy, but the prevention margin is not as wide as it was in Q2. Winter respiratory demand, school absences, and continued record-transfer delays kept the immunization rate close to the threshold.
periods.recommendations: Protect the remaining margin by setting a 30-day action list for every child in the registry who is one dose overdue, with outreach divided by clinic panel and school attendance zone. Keep two nurse-led evening clinics at Seaside Family Center and add a Saturday site at Driftwood Middle School before the spring semester. For life expectancy, review Q4 mortality and injury data with EMS and the hospital partners to confirm whether the decline reflects normal variation or a preventable pattern.

periods.analysis: Q1 shows stabilization after the narrow Q4 margin: childhood immunization increased from 95.4% to 95.9%, a 0.5-point quarter-over-quarter improvement and still above the >=95% target. Life expectancy held steady at 81.3 years, unchanged from Q4 and above the >=80-year target. The Driftwood Saturday clinic and provider-panel outreach appear to have recovered children who were overdue after winter absences. This is green performance with a practical lesson: Harborview does best when prevention is brought close to schools, clinics, and family schedules.
periods.recommendations: Continue the school-adjacent clinic model through spring, prioritizing Driftwood, East Bluff Elementary, and Marina View K-8 based on overdue counts. Ask each major pediatric provider to close its top 25 open immunization gaps before the end of April and report barriers to the Health Department. Maintain the life expectancy prevention bundle, with special focus on hypertension, fall risk, and opioid-overdose prevention as standing quarterly review items.

periods.analysis: By Q2, Harborview is back to a wide green margin: childhood immunization increased from 95.9% to 97.6%, a 1.7-point quarter-over-quarter gain and well above the >=95% target. Life expectancy increased from 81.3 years to 81.6 years, a 0.3-year gain and above the >=80-year target. The chronological pattern is clear: the city absorbed growth, corrected record gaps, and regained prevention coverage through targeted clinics and provider accountability. This is the strongest combined close since the start of the period, with both measures moving in the right direction.
periods.recommendations: Lock in the gain by making the New Resident Vaccine Welcome workflow and school-adjacent clinics permanent elements of the Public Health operating calendar. Expand the provider missed-opportunity report to include adolescent boosters and schedule quarterly data-quality audits with the three largest pediatric groups. Use the improved life expectancy position to deepen prevention work, not relax it: fund the next cycle of walking prescriptions, blood pressure kiosks, and overdose-reversal training in the highest-need census tracts.

periods.analysis: June immunization coverage of 97.6% and life expectancy of 81.6 years both exceeded their targets. Those figures are carried forward, however, and do not establish new September outcomes. Completed back-to-school clinics show delivery progress, not yet a measured change in population health.
periods.recommendations: Validate the September immunization registry and the next available life-expectancy release before confirming this objective's Q3 outcome. Use the separate Community Health Improvement Plan's established outcome reporting as a cross-scorecard walkthrough, without treating its update cycle as this scorecard's data source.
